steps.title: Validate prediction request and response schemas

blocks.text: Parseable JSON can still violate a prediction contract. Decode first; acceptance also needs field, value and response-alignment checks.
The request schema specifies features, types and permitted values; the response schema specifies output structure.
Decode JSON into Python values before checking field presence and types. Raw text is not the structured request.
Compare required versus supplied key sets, then test declared types and numeric boundaries with conditional predicates.
For matrix-valued inputs, construct the declared NumPy representation and verify rank, feature width and output row alignment against the request/response contract.
Reject malformed or out-of-contract requests explicitly rather than returning a successful prediction from invalid inputs.
Assert the declared valid, boundary and failure predicates. In ordinary non-optimized execution, a false assertion raises AssertionError.

blocks.code:
# Symbolic checks against the supplied contract, not computed output.
body = json.dumps(request_values).encode("utf-8")
request = json.loads(body)
assert set(request) == set(contract["request_keys"])
values = reject_malformed(request)  # checks declared types and bounds
matrix = np.array(values, dtype=contract["numpy_dtype"])
assert matrix.ndim == contract["matrix_rank"]
assert matrix.shape[1] == contract["matrix_width"]
response = json.loads(response_body)
assert set(response) == set(contract["response_keys"])
assert len(response["predictions"]) == matrix.shape[0]
# Use valid, boundary and rejected fixtures; decoding alone is not acceptance.

steps.title: Encode and send the JSON request

blocks.text: Send a JSON request body as encoded bytes in urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST"), then read the response through urlopen with a stated timeout.
Serialize structured request/response values with json.dumps; decode JSON with json.loads before inspecting fields.

steps.title: Validate decoded request and response contracts

blocks.text: In the order fixture, decode the body before checking required keys, numeric types, permitted bounds and matrix dimensions. Check the decoded response separately for required output keys and one output per request row. A missing key must be rejected before prediction; an included boundary and a value beyond it are different test cases. Serialize the request, send encoded bytes with the JSON header and stated timeout, then decode the response. Parsing, schema acceptance and output correctness are separate assertions.

steps.title: Distinguish JSON decoding from schema acceptance

blocks.text: Raw JSON text is not the structured request, and successful JSON decoding is not schema acceptance. A response with the wrong row correspondence still violates the prediction contract.

blocks.text: A running process may still lack initialized prediction assets. Readiness must describe whether inference can be accepted.

Return a successful readiness result only after the model is loaded and the service can accept inference, not merely after process startup.

steps.title: Reproduce a model deployment from parameterized runtime configuration and an immutable artifact reference

blocks.text: Prepare repeatable configuration before applying it. Separate nonsecret settings from runtime secret references.
Pin deployment to the recorded immutable image digest; a mutable tag may later resolve to different contents.

In the supplied Docker Compose runtime, author the mapping services: {prediction: {image: IMAGE_DIGEST, environment: {SETTING: VALUE}, ports: ["HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT"], secrets: [credential], deploy: {replicas: REPLICA_COUNT}}} and top-level secrets: {credential: {environment: INJECTED_SECRET_VARIABLE}}; substitute the approved digest, nonsecret setting, port numbers, supported replica count and host secret-variable name, never the secret value.
Set a service’s image to its immutable artifact reference, its ports to HOST:CONTAINER mappings, and its environment to the declared nonsecret key/value settings.

left.title: Authored configuration
left.alt_text: Recorded immutable image → HOST:CONTAINER ports; nonsecret environment → Runtime secret-variable reference → Supported replica/resource bounds → Safely reloaded YAML → compose config

right.title: Observed runtime

nodes.label: Compare actual identity and runtime settings
Destroy only test deployment; reapply same file
Verify identical artifact and resolved settings

blocks.takeaway: Parsed configuration is not proof of running identity; runtime support for deploy fields must be checked.

blocks.code:
import json
with open("runtime_contract.json") as source:
    intended = json.load(source)
# Inspect live fixture execution separately from the intended configuration.

# Check State and Health when configured, plus sanitized initialization/execution logs.
# Bounded readiness and prediction checks must verify status and decoded payload.
# Do not interpret launch success as acceptance.

# Safely write/reload; resolve fields before application.

Secret references name injected variables, never credential values.

Authentication establishes the caller identity and authorization checks whether that identity may perform the prediction action; both are needed for the supplied protected service.
Reference the protected credential through an authorized runtime secret, and give it only to the service permitted to use it rather than writing its literal value in the YAML.
Inject the platform’s declared nonsecret authentication settings in the service configuration, keeping them separate from the credential secret.
Make one request with the authorized supplied credential and negative requests with missing or invalid credentials; verify allowed and denied responses under the existing platform policy.
Inspect runtime logs to verify failures are visible without displaying the credential or protected request values.
A Compose YAML document declares services by name; use indented mappings for service fields and lists or mappings in the forms required by the Compose specification.

steps.title: Resolve authentication runtime settings

blocks.text: Set a service’s image to its immutable artifact reference, its ports to HOST:CONTAINER mappings, and its environment to the declared nonsecret key/value settings.
Use docker compose -f CONFIG_PATH config to parse, resolve and validate the authored YAML before applying it; check its resolved fields against the intended runtime contract.
Apply the declared local Compose deployment with docker compose -f CONFIG_PATH up -d and inspect the resulting containers.

steps.title: Verify tokens and permitted subjects

blocks.text: For the supplied Google ID-token verifier contract, use from google.oauth2 import id_token and from google.auth.transport import requests; implement authorize_prediction(token, expected_audience, permitted_subjects) to reject a missing token, call claims = id_token.verify_oauth2_token(token, requests.Request(), audience=expected_audience), and return the verified claims only when claims["sub"] is in the supplied permitted_subjects policy, otherwise raising PermissionError. Use the verified sub identity, not an unverified decode or a changeable email address.
Assert the declared valid, boundary and failure predicates. In ordinary non-optimized execution, a false assertion raises AssertionError.

With the declared PyYAML dependency, import yaml; write a mapping/list configuration with yaml.safe_dump(config, file_handle), reload it with yaml.safe_load(file_handle), and inspect the required resolved fields before submitting it to the existing runtime. Safe loading supports standard YAML tags, not arbitrary Python object constructors.

steps.title: Reject unauthorized requests before prediction

blocks.text: Use from google.auth.exceptions import GoogleAuthError; catch (ValueError, GoogleAuthError) from verification and raise PermissionError for the service harness’s declared denied HTTP path before calling prediction; a ValueError signals verification failure and GoogleAuthError includes invalid issuer. Missing credentials, invalid tokens and verified-but-unpermitted subjects must all be denied without executing prediction or logging the token.

Use the supplied audience and permitted-subject policy. Reject a missing token; verify an offered token, then check verified sub membership. A verified but unpermitted subject is denied too. Convert declared verification exceptions into the denied HTTP path before prediction. Safely inspect Compose image, ports, nonsecret settings and runtime secret references. Test authorized, missing, invalid and unpermitted fixtures. Denied requests must neither execute prediction nor disclose tokens in logs.
Authentication does not automatically grant authorization. A verified-but-unpermitted subject must be denied, and neither YAML nor logs should contain the credential's literal value.

Instrument prediction-service availability, errors and latency

blocks.text: Client outcomes can differ from handler records. Reconcile external requests with handler timing, including attempts that never arrived.
Choose client-visible request outcomes and latency as service indicators instead of inferring availability only from container or CPU state.
Measure an attempt’s elapsed time as time.perf_counter() after completion minus its start value, retaining a consistent duration unit.
Record enough timestamped outcome and duration evidence to distinguish successes, errors and timeouts in the measurement window.
Compute an error fraction as error attempts divided by eligible attempts, using the same clearly declared observation window and denominator as the success indicator.
Estimate client-visible success probability as successful eligible attempts divided by all eligible attempts in the defined measurement window, counting failed attempts in the denominator.
Use np.mean(numeric_values) for the arithmetic mean of the selected numeric observations.

blocks.caption: Authored offline attempts: reconcile client outcomes with handler timestamps and absent handler records. These are not production measurements.

steps.title: Count every scheduled probe attempt

blocks.text: Use np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0): divide squared deviations by N, then take the square root. Use ddof=1 only when the declared calculation requires N−1.
Instrument the handler around JSON decoding, prediction and JSON response encoding, recording duration and status/error counts even on its handled error paths.
For the prescribed probe, retain its half-open five-minute window [t0, t0+300 seconds), its one valid request per second and all 300 attempt outcomes.
Count an attempt as available only for an HTTP 200 response with a valid prediction received within its two-second deadline; allow the final attempt its entire deadline before summarizing.
Compute availability as that successful-deadline count divided by 300, including connection-refused and response-timeout attempts that never reach the handler.
Reconcile absent handler records with the external failure record and report the probe window, numerator and denominator alongside handler latency/statistics and status counts.

steps.title: Separate probe availability from handler telemetry

blocks.text: For the prescribed probe, retain every scheduled attempt, including connection refusals and timeouts with no handler record. Count only valid successful predictions received by the deadline, allowing the final attempt its full deadline before summarizing. Report the window, successful-deadline numerator and full attempt denominator. Reconcile missing handler events with external failures. Handler timing covers JSON decoding, prediction and encoding, including handled error paths; its success rate alone is not client-visible availability.
Handler success rate is not automatically client-visible availability. Excluding attempts that never reached the handler would omit part of the prescribed denominator and conceal failures.

steps.title: Load-test a prediction endpoint against tail-latency and sustainable-throughput objectives

blocks.text: Measure a capacity envelope from client outcomes, tail latency, completed work and backlog at each declared load.
Exercise the endpoint with the declared arrival/concurrency profile and bounded duration, and record client-visible outcomes and response times rather than only attempted request count.
Treat a load point as acceptable only if it meets the predeclared client-visible success and tail-latency requirements, as well as the required completed throughput.
Retain failures and timeouts separately so latency measured only for completed responses is not misrepresented as the experience of every attempted request.
Estimate client-visible success probability as successful eligible attempts divided by all eligible attempts in the defined measurement window, counting failed attempts in the denominator.
Compute the declared tail-latency percentile with np.percentile(completed_latency_values, declared_percentile), retaining its convention, sample count and time unit.
Measure successful throughput as completed successful requests divided by elapsed measurement time, and compare it with the offered load rather than equating arrivals with completed work.

blocks.caption: Authored offline attempts include multiple experiment settings. Select the declared valid-traffic load population before calculating capacity; retain errors and timeouts.

Compute failed-request fraction from all failed attempts divided by all valid-traffic attempts; timeouts remain failures.

Inspect backlog growth and unfinished work throughout the window; accept only stable-backlog loads meeting the predeclared tail-latency and error limits, and report the highest measured successful throughput or no feasible measured envelope.

blocks.text: Inspect the registered valid-traffic attempts alongside unfinished work. Keep HTTP errors, timeouts and other failures separate, but include all valid attempts in success and failed-fraction denominators. Calculate successful completions per measurement time, not arrivals per time. Percentiles describe completed-response samples with declared units and convention, not timed-out responses. Accept only stable-backlog points meeting all declared latency, error and throughput objectives, or report no feasible measured envelope. Intentional malformed fixtures stay outside this capacity population.

steps.title: Match batching responses and full request latency

blocks.text: For each registered trace row, decode the successful response and match its request identity and batching setting before calculating duration. Measure request start through response completion, including the waiting interval. Compute the declared percentile, mean and spread over matched successful responses, retaining units, convention and sample count. Compare settings using that same population interpretation and choose only a measured limit meeting the objective. A shorter execution interval cannot compensate for a full request interval that misses the latency limit.

Configure bounded prediction-worker concurrency on an existing runtime

blocks.text: A worker limit in YAML is intent. Inspect whether running workers honor it during the bounded load.
A Compose YAML document declares services by name; use indented mappings for service fields and lists or mappings in the forms required by the Compose specification.
Set a service’s image to its immutable artifact reference, its ports to HOST:CONTAINER mappings, and its environment to the declared nonsecret key/value settings.
Use docker compose -f CONFIG_PATH config to parse, resolve and validate the authored YAML before applying it; check its resolved fields against the intended runtime contract.
Apply the declared local Compose deployment with docker compose -f CONFIG_PATH up -d and inspect the resulting containers.
Set the existing runtime’s worker-limit setting in the YAML, validate its parsed value and run the referenced image under that bound.
Inspect running worker processes with docker container top NAME during the load fixture and compare the observed count with the configured limit to detect oversubscription.

left.code:
# Approved changed configuration (intent, not process evidence)
config = {'services': {'prediction': {'image': 'fixture.local/orders@sha256:29371dd36fb111803c6fe996426f342680170dec59168e1e52139cdb4fbfaf83', 'environment': {'MODE': 'fixture', 'WORKER_LIMIT': '2'}, 'ports': ['8080:8080'], 'secrets': ['credential']}}, 'secrets': {'credential': {'environment': 'ORDER_FIXTURE_CREDENTIAL'}}}

right.caption: Authored process evidence: distinguish prediction workers from supervisor processes; align interval_id with resource observations.

blocks.takeaway: Safely reload and resolve the changed worker limit, then compare actual prediction workers with that bound and inspect same-interval CPU/memory.

blocks.caption: Authored CPU/memory observations: align interval_id with the process evidence.

blocks.code:
import json, yaml
with open("runtime_contract.json") as source:
    runtime = json.load(source)
service = config["services"][runtime["SERVICE"]]
service["environment"][runtime["worker_limit_key"]] = str(runtime["approved_worker_limit"])
with open(runtime["CONFIG_PATH"], "w") as target:
    yaml.safe_dump(config, target)
with open(runtime["CONFIG_PATH"]) as source:
    reloaded = yaml.safe_load(source)
assert int(reloaded["services"][runtime["SERVICE"]]["environment"][runtime["worker_limit_key"]]) == runtime["approved_worker_limit"]
# Resolve with compose config; apply and compare observed workers with this bound.

steps.title: Roll back a serving release to a previous approved registry artifact

blocks.text: Resolve the approved previous artifact. Verify its replacement service before retiring the faulty test release.
Resolve the previously approved registry version and its artifact as the rollback target, preserving the approval/version identity rather than selecting an unapproved latest version.
Use the recorded previous immutable image reference for the approved replacement container.
Verify readiness and a bounded prediction fixture after the rollback, and confirm the response contract still matches the service.
Keep secrets out of Dockerfile ARG and ENV: they persist in the final image or its metadata.
Deliver sensitive values through runtime secrets, never as literal Compose values.
Start the approved replacement under its distinct container identity with the required environment and published port; do not retire the faulty test release before the replacement is ready.

before.caption: Authored approval records identify the previous immutable replacement; the faulty test release is still running.

after.caption: Authored chronology, not live command evidence: replacement is verified before faulty-release retirement.

blocks.change_summary: Start the approved replacement under its distinct identity; inspect State, available Health and sanitized logs, then verify readiness and decoded prediction/version before stopping and removing only the faulty test release.

steps.title: Verify replacement endpoints before retiring the faulty release

blocks.text: After replacement readiness and a verified JSON prediction/version response, stop and remove only the faulty test release, preserving the approved replacement.

Send a JSON request body as encoded bytes in urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST"), then read the response through urlopen with a stated timeout.
Serialize structured request/response values with json.dumps; decode JSON with json.loads before inspecting fields.
Inspect the running container identity and State, including Health when a healthcheck is configured, and compare them with the intended release.
Inspect runtime logs for initialization and execution failures without copying sensitive request data or credentials into the evidence record.
Call the declared readiness and prediction endpoints with bounded timeouts and check the returned status and payload against the expected contracts.

steps.title: Trace the approved rollback replacement

blocks.text: Keep the faulty test release running while starting the approved previous release under its distinct identity and published port. Resolve the recorded immutable artifact rather than latest. Inspect replacement State, available Health and sanitized logs. With bounded calls, verify readiness and decoded JSON prediction/version against the contract. Only then stop and remove the faulty test release, preserving the replacement. Keep credentials runtime-injected, not in image metadata, Compose values or evidence.
Rollback is not ‘use latest’ or remove everything old. The target must retain its approval/version identity, and the faulty test release is not retired before replacement readiness.
